(a) slicing localization (Steps 1–5 and the first half of Step 10): near each x₀, ∂R agrees with ∂(R⌞B_r(x₀)) on forms supported in B_r(x₀), and R⌞B_r(x₀) is integer multiplicity with finite mass and finite boundary mass;
(b) extension by zero of that piece to ℝ^P (Step 6);
(c) comparison of the masses of the extension with those of its restriction, via (VO) (Step 6);
(d) boundary rectifiability in ℝ^P for a compactly supported IM current of finite mass and boundary mass, from (DT) and CL(d) (Steps 7–9; Simon Ch. 6, 6.2 first case and 6.3).
Unsplit, the node would formalize all of these inline. It would also need the IMRep measure calculus, the mass ≤ representing-measure bound, a smooth-cutoff argument and the evaluation bound: several hundred Lean lines. Kernel-checked equivalents of the helpers already exist in this run, so five children are reuses and only three new DAG nodes are created.

 (i) Part (1) of cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local for X := ∂R (locally finite mass by hbd) reduces the goal to this: every x₀ ∈ U has r > 0 and h : B_r(x₀) ⊆ U with (∂R).restrictDomain h integer multiplicity.

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous. This is the comparator-accepted declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props, reused at its byte-identical frozen type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this child is the comparator-accepted declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, candidate f492ba4a003c8f1324077e050d48667ae23c7100), taken at its byte-identical frozen type. The runtime keeps an accepted checkpoint as it is, so this reuse creates no node and no new proof work. Its accepted Lean proof was recompiled in this session against the frozen contract; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Use in this decomposition: deformation_closure, step 3: part (iv), continuity of |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, gives a finite bound sup_x |ω(x)| for every test form ω on ℝ^P. The reviewed proof follows.
Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition
N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. Coefficient vector. For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), together with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives
   N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F.   (∗)

2. Linearity of v. Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So, coordinatewise, c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α); both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).

3. Proof of (i). By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙:
   N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').

4. Proof of (ii). By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm:
   N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).

5. Coordinate bound. For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
   - If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖.
   - Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.

6. Proof of (iii). Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0,
   N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.

7. Proof of (iv). Let α, α' ∈ F.
   - By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α').
   - α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg, or (ii) with t = −1). So by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α).
   Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. Thus dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α', so N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.

Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with the constant C of (iii) equal to √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
(i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

Therefore spt Y ⊆ K, which is (ii). Consequently spt Y = K ∖ Z_Y: ⊆ by (ii), and ⊇ because K ⊆ V ⊆ U. Z_Y is open (isOpen_zeroRegion), so K ∖ Z_Y is compact (IsCompact.diff), which is (iii).
7. (Boundary, (iv).) If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes Y holds by definition. Let n = m + 1 and ∂X = 0 in V; we show ∂Y = 0.
 - Cutoff. Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior (model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), smoothness ⊤ : ℕ∞, closed set K ⊆ thickening δ K ⊆ interior (cthickening δ K)), then contMDiff_iff_contDiff. This gives a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on an open O ⊇ K (mem_nhdsSet_iff_exists) and χ = 0 outside cthickening δ K. So tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ V, and tsupport χ is compact.
 - For ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U), χω := (x ↦ χ(x)ω(x)) is smooth (ContDiff.smul) with tsupport(χω) ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ V. So χω ∈ 𝒟^m(V).
 - χω = ω on the open set O, so d(χω)(x) = dω(x) for every x ∈ O: the exterior derivative at x depends only on the germ at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq).
 - The carrier M ∩ K ⊆ K ⊆ O, so the integrands of R'.action(dω) and R'.action(d(χω)) agree on it (setIntegral_congr_fun). Hence ∂Y(ω) = Y(dω) = R'.action(dω) = R'.action(d(χω)) = R.action(d(χω)) = X(d(χω)) = ∂X(χω) = 0. Here we used step 2, that R represents X, and that d(χω) is the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn V m (χω).
 Hence ∂Y = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes Y. ∎
proof_key_steps: R' := (M ∩ K, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U with R'.action = R.action, because M ∩ K and M differ by an Hⁿ-null set and approximate tangent planes ignore null modifications.
The integral functional of an IMRep is a current (sup-norm bound against ∫_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ on a fixed compact C); let Y := τ(R'). Y is integer multiplicity and restricts to X on 𝒟ⁿ(V).
Y kills forms whose support misses K, so spt Y ⊆ K and spt Y = K ∖ Z_Y is compact.
If ∂X = 0, a cutoff χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) equal to 1 near K gives ∂Y(ω) = R'.action(d(χω)) = X(d(χω)) = ∂X(χω) = 0.

They are the exact frozen statements of cmc_exists_massRepresentation, the second and fourth conjuncts of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, and cmc_slice_mass_bounds. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a representation (μ, ξ) with μ finite on compact subsets of U, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ (plus further properties not used here). (IMC)(b) for an IMRep (M, θ, ξ) of U and a measurable E there is an IMRep of U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. (IMC)(d) the orientation of an IMRep satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x. (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) represented by (μ, ξ) with ∂X represented by (μ', ξ') gives A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' in U, with ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η misses {f = t}, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W (and a pointwise liminf bound not used here). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) integer multiplicity with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and x₀ ∈ U. Then there are r > 0 with closedBall(x₀, r) ⊆ U, a current R' ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) and an IMRep R'' of U representing R' with carrier ⊆ B_r(x₀), such that M(R') < ∞, M(∂R') < ∞ (M = mass in U), and ∂R'(η) = ∂R(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀).

Source: parent proof, Steps 1–5 and the first half of Step 10 (Simon Ch. 6, 4.5(1)–(2): for a Lipschitz f, T⌞{f < t} has boundary of finite mass for L¹-a.e. t; 6.2, general case: cut T at such a level so that the piece has finite boundary mass). Uses the siblings lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict (key imrep_restrict) and lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact (key vanish_off_compact), both comparator-accepted declarations reused at their frozen types.
Notation: |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ("admissible for M_W"). M(X) = M_U(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.mass). B_t(x₀) = ball x₀ t, H = μHE[d + 1], and ξ(ω) denotes x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)).
Change from the supplied text: step 5 takes the good radius from the integrated bound of (SL), not from the measure-convergence tool (MM) of cbr_measure_convergence_tools applied to the constant sequence μ_j = μ. The integrated bound gives a radius directly and needs no measurability of t ↦ M_G(∂A_t − B_t).
0. Mass is bounded by a representing measure (Step 0(iii) of the parent proof). Let k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(U), ν a measure on ℝ^P and ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P). Assume |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for ν-a.e. x and all k-covectors α, and X(ω) = ∫ ζ(ω) dν for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Then M_W(X) ≤ ν(W) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P. Proof: let ω be admissible for M_W and g := ζ(ω). Then ofReal(X(ω)) = ofReal(∫ g dν) ≤ ‖∫ g dν‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). This holds without integrability, because the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0. Now take ν-a.e. x. If x ∈ W, then ‖g(x)‖ₑ = ofReal|ζ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ofReal|ω(x)| ≤ 1. If x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and g(x) = ζ(x)(0) = 0. Hence ‖g‖ₑ ≤ 1_W ν-a.e., and ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν ≤ ∫⁻ 1_W dν ≤ ν(W) (lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_indicator_one_le; W need not be measurable). Taking the supremum over admissible ω proves the claim.
1. Representation of R. R is integer multiplicity, so some IMRep R₀ = (M, θ, ξ) of U represents R: R(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH for ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U). Put μ := R₀.measure = (H⌞M).withDensity θ. By lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict:
 (a) μ ≪ H⌞M;
 (b) ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable;
 (c) R′.action(ω) = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ for every Borel E ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R′ of U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ, and every (d+1)-form ω.
 μ is finite on compact subsets of U. Let K ⊆ U be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so μ(K) = ∫⁻_K θ d(H⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). The IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult makes this finite.
 By (IMC)(d), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α and H⌞M-a.e. x; by (a) this also holds for μ-a.e. x (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le).
 Finally take E := ℝ^P and R′ := R₀ in (c); this is allowed because the carrier of R₀ is M = M ∩ ℝ^P. It gives R₀.action(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P} ξ(ω) dμ = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ (Measure.restrict_univ). Hence R(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U).
2. Representation of ∂R. ∂R ∈ 𝒟_d(U), and M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U. So (REP) gives a measure μ' and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_d(ℝ^P) such that:
 - μ'(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U;
 - ξ' is μ'-a.e. strongly measurable;
 - |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α;
 - ∂R(η) = ∫ ξ'(η) dμ' for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U).
3. A radius r₀. U is open and x₀ ∈ U, so there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x₀) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put r₀ := ε/2 > 0. Then closedBall(x₀, r₀) ⊆ B_ε(x₀) ⊆ U, and closedBall(x₀, r₀) is compact. By steps 1–2, μ(closedBall(x₀, r₀)) < ∞ and μ'(closedBall(x₀, r₀)) < ∞.
4. Slicing. Let f(x) := dist(x, x₀) = |x − x₀|. It is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.dist_left), {x : f(x) < t} = B_t(x₀) and {x : f(x) = t} = sphere(x₀, t). Apply (SL) with k := d, T := R, the pairs (μ, ξ) and (μ', ξ') of steps 1–2, f and L := 1. Its hypotheses hold:
 - U is open;
 - μ and μ' are finite on compact subsets of U;
 - ξ and ξ' are a.e. strongly measurable;
 - |ξ| ≤ |·| μ-a.e. (step 1), and |ξ'| ≤ |·| everywhere, hence μ'-a.e.;
 - R and ∂R are represented as required.
 This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with:
 (i) A_t(ω) = ∫_{B_t(x₀)} ξ(ω) dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U);
 (ii) B_t(η) = ∫_{B_t(x₀)} ξ'(η) dμ' for η ∈ 𝒟^d(U);
 (iii) ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η is disjoint from sphere(x₀, t);
 (iv) ∫⁻_{t∈(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for every open W and all a, b ∈ ℝ (as L = 1).
5. A good radius. Let G := B_{r₀}(x₀) and apply (iv) with W := G, a := 0, b := r₀. The right side is at most μ(closedBall(x₀, r₀)) < ∞, because G ∩ {0 < f < r₀} ⊆ G ⊆ closedBall(x₀, r₀). Suppose M_G(∂A_t − B_t) = ∞ for every t ∈ (0, r₀). Then the left side is ∫⁻_{(0,r₀)} ∞ dt = ∞·L¹((0, r₀)) = ∞·r₀ = ∞ (setLIntegral_congr_fun on the measurable set (0, r₀), lintegral_const, Real.volume_Ioo, r₀ > 0). This is a contradiction. Hence there is r ∈ (0, r₀) with M_G(Z) < ∞, where Z := ∂A_r − B_r ∈ 𝒟_d(U).
6. Total mass of Z. Let η ∈ 𝒟^d(U) have tsupport η disjoint from sphere(x₀, r). Then Z(η) = ∂A_r(η) − B_r(η) = 0 by (iii). The sphere is compact (isCompact_sphere) and lies in the open set G, because r < r₀. Apply lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact with C := sphere(x₀, r), V := G, X := Z and the arbitrary set U. It gives M(Z) = M_U(Z) ≤ M_G(Z) < ∞.
7. Mass of B_r. By (ii), B_r(η) = ∫ ξ'(η) d(μ'⌞B_r(x₀)) for η ∈ 𝒟^d(U). The bound |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| holds everywhere, hence μ'⌞B_r(x₀)-a.e. Step 0 with k := d, ν := μ'⌞B_r(x₀), ζ := ξ' and W := U gives M(B_r) ≤ (μ'⌞B_r(x₀))(U) ≤ μ'(B_r(x₀)) ≤ μ'(closedBall(x₀, r₀)) < ∞.
8. Mass of ∂A_r. For every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U), ∂A_r(η) = B_r(η) + Z(η), since Z(η) = ∂A_r(η) − B_r(η). Let η be admissible for M_U. Then ofReal(∂A_r(η)) ≤ ofReal(B_r(η)) + ofReal(Z(η)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le) ≤ M_U(B_r) + M_U(Z) (le_massOn). Taking the supremum, M(∂A_r) ≤ M(B_r) + M(Z), which is finite by steps 6–7.
9. A_r is represented by an IMRep with carrier in B_r(x₀). Apply (IMC)(b) to R₀ and E := B_r(x₀), which is open and hence Borel. It gives an IMRep R'' of U with carrier M ∩ B_r(x₀), multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U). Step 1(c) with E := B_r(x₀) and R′ := R'' gives R''.action(ω) = ∫_{B_r(x₀)} ξ(ω) dμ, and this is A_r(ω) by (i). So R'' represents R' := A_r, and its carrier M ∩ B_r(x₀) is contained in B_r(x₀).
10. Mass of R'. By (i), A_r(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) d(μ⌞B_r(x₀)). The bound |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| holds μ-a.e. (step 1), hence μ⌞B_r(x₀)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae). Step 0 with k := d + 1, ν := μ⌞B_r(x₀) and W := U gives M(R') ≤ (μ⌞B_r(x₀))(U) ≤ μ(B_r(x₀)) ≤ μ(closedBall(x₀, r₀)) < ∞.
11. Agreement with ∂R. Let η ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀). Points of B_r(x₀) have distance < r from x₀, so tsupport η is disjoint from sphere(x₀, r). Hence ∂R'(η) = ∂A_r(η) = B_r(η) by (iii), and B_r(η) = ∫_{B_r(x₀)} ξ'(η) dμ' by (ii). This equals ∫ ξ'(η) dμ', because the integrand vanishes off B_r(x₀): there x ∉ tsupport η, so η(x) = 0 and ξ'(x)(0) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). By step 2 it equals ∂R(η).
12. Conclusion. We have r > 0 and closedBall(x₀, r) ⊆ closedBall(x₀, r₀) ⊆ U, as r < r₀. Take R' = A_r and R''. Then R'' represents R' with carrier ⊆ B_r(x₀) (step 9), M(R') < ∞ (step 10) and M(∂R') < ∞ (step 8). Also ∂R'(η) = ∂R(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U) supported in B_r(x₀) (step 11). ∎
